title: What do these rules generate?
hook: Generate four worlds, then replace one variable’s assignment rule.

claims.text: Independent fair binary Z,U generate X=Z+U and Y=2X+Z. After intervening to set X=1 for every world, what is mean Y?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-structural-equations/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Enumerate Z,U independent fairbinary, X=Z+U,Y=2X+Z. Four worlds (Z,U,X,Y):0000,0112,1013,1125. InterveneX=1 producesY2or3 regardlessU.

claims.text: The intervention retains mean Y=2.5 and fixes every X at 1. The natural equations retain outcomes ranging from 0 to 5.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-structural-equations/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Enumerate Z,U independent fairbinary, X=Z+U,Y=2X+Z. Four worlds (Z,U,X,Y):0000,0112,1013,1125. InterveneX=1 producesY2or3 regardlessU.

claims.text: An intervention replaces the X equation; it does not regenerate Z or U. The unchanged upstream worlds feed into the revised outcome rule, which is why the remaining Y variation comes only from Z here.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-structural-equations/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Enumerate Z,U independent fairbinary, X=Z+U,Y=2X+Z. Four worlds (Z,U,X,Y):0000,0112,1013,1125. InterveneX=1 producesY2or3 regardlessU.

claims.text: For Y=3X+Z, with fair binary Z, setting X=2 gives which mean Y? The intervention fixes 3X=6 and leaves mean Z=.5, giving mean Y=6.5.
